manufacturer_data.description: Observed on a real ID107 HR (g7smy.co.uk BlueZ session): company ID 0x001C with a payload containing the band's own public MAC address (e.g. C5:E8:FB:AA:BB:CC) followed by a trailing byte. A matching 0xAF0 advertisement is the far stronger signal; treat this as corroboration only.

device.manufacturer: Unknown ODM (ID107-class bands sold under Makibes and many other brands; companion app Veryfit 2.0)
device.name: Veryfit 2.0 Fitness Band (ID107 / ID111 class)
device.notes:
The ID107/ID111-class fitness bands (~2016 generation, Nordic nRF51822 SoC, Si1142 optical heart-rate sensor, Kionix kx022 accelerometer — per public hardware notes) are driven by the Veryfit 2.0 Android app (Veryfit 2.0). The bands advertise as e.g. "ID107 HR" with manufacturer data under company ID 0x001C embedding the device's own public MAC address, and expose a single vendor GATT service 00000af0 (confirmed on the wire by g7smy.co.uk's BlueZ session with a real band).
All commands and responses are 20-byte fixed frames, zero-padded: byte 0 = command ID, byte 1 = key, bytes 2..19 = key-specific payload (max 18 bytes; DeviceBaseCommand in the app zero-fills the frame and copies the payload starting at byte 2). Normal commands are written to 00000af6 and answered on 00000af7; health-data sync (command ID 0x08) runs over the parallel channel 00000af1 (write) / 00000af2 (notify) — the app routes any frame whose command ID is 0x08 to the health channel.
Command IDs (from the app's base command table): firmware update 0x01, get-info 0x02, settings 0x03, bind/unbind 0x04, phone→band notify 0x05, app control 0x06, BLE control 0x07, health data 0x08, dump-stack 0x20, log 0x21, restart 0xF0, factory 0xAA. Get-info keys: basic 0x01, function 0x02, time 0x03, MAC 0x04, battery 0x05, real-time 0xA0. Settings keys: time 0x01, alarm 0x02, multi-target 0x03, user info 0x10, units 0x11, sedentary 0x20, anti-lost 0x21, hand 0x22, OS 0x23, HR range 0x24, HR mode 0x25, find-phone 0x26, one-key restore 0x27, wrist gesture 0x28, DND 0x29, music 0x2A, H/V mode 0x2B, telegram 0x30, message 0x31. Notify keys: incoming call 0x01, call status 0x02, message 0x03, missed message 0x04; the message key's payload tags the source app (WeChat 0x03, QQ 0x04, Facebook 0x06, Twitter 0x07, WhatsApp 0x08, Messenger 0x09, Instagram 0x0A, LinkedIn 0x0B). App-control keys: mic 0x01, camera 0x02, single-sport 0x03, find-band 0x04. Payload layouts beyond the key byte (set-time layout, real-time field offsets, notification text encoding) are NOT established — the 2026-07 review of this analysis marked all byte-level payload formats unverifiable without an HCI snoop; only the frame shape and the key tables are solid.
Health-data sync (cmd 0x08 on the af1/af2 channel) keys: sync request 0x01, sync success 0x02, per-type data: sports-today 0x03, sleep-today 0x04, sports-history 0x05, sleep-history 0x06, heart-rate-today 0x07, heart-rate-history 0x08, send-finished 0xEE, error 0xFF. Sync frames carry a mode byte (safe 0x01 / other 0x00), a flag byte (foreground 0x01 / background 0x02) and a status (start 0x01 / resend 0x03 / end 0x02).
OTA is the Nordic legacy buttonless DFU (service 00001530-…): the app bundles no.nordicsemi.android.dfu and declares its DfuService. The DFU characteristics are only present while the band is in its bootloader — the on-wire capture of a running ID107 HR shows only GAP/GATT plus the 0xAF0 service.
SECURITY: no pairing, bonding or authentication exists anywhere in the app protocol; any client in range can read the band's health history and user data.
No Gadgetbridge support exists for the Veryfit/ID107 protocol family (Gadgetbridge's cheap-band support covers the unrelated FitPro family instead), and no other open-source implementation of this protocol was found — the vendor app is the only known client.
IMPORTANT — this is NOT the protocol of the "M6 Smart Fitness Band" (Telink TLSR8232 / LT716 platform, FitPro app, Nordic UART Service + 0xCD frames): the stock M6 firmware contains no 0xAF0 UUID anywhere. This analysis was briefly mis-attributed to the M6; see device-specs/devices/m6-fitness-band.yaml.

credentials.notes: BLE-only; no credentials of any kind cross the link and there is no authentication, so the band's stored health data is readable by anyone in radio range.

factory_reset.effect: The app exposes a "one-key restore" settings command (cmd 0x03, key 0x27), i.e. an over-the-air factory reset exists — but its payload bytes beyond the key are not established, and what exactly it clears (user profile, stored health data, bind state) is unknown. A separate command ID 0xAA (factory) exists in the app and is likewise undocumented at the byte level. No hardware button procedure is known.

procedures.basis: Read from the vendor app's settings command table, not run against hardware: the app exposes a "one-key restore" as settings command 0x03 with key 0x27, and a separate command id 0xAA labelled factory. Neither frame's payload bytes beyond the key were established, so a client must expect to work the encoding out.
procedures.name: One-key restore over BLE (candidate)

steps.action: Open the band's settings characteristic and send the settings command 0x03 with key 0x27.
steps.expect: Unestablished. What it clears — user profile, stored health data, bind state — was never observed.

methods.description: Scan for service 00000af0 (local name typically "ID107 HR"-style), connect over GATT, enable notifications on 00000af7, send the bind frame, then drive the band with 20-byte command/key frames written to 00000af6 (health sync: 00000af1, answers on 00000af2).

steps.action: Scan for advertisements carrying service UUID 00000af0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (name prefix ID107) and connect.
steps.expect: GATT table with service 00000af0 and characteristics af6 (write), af7 (notify), af1 (write), af2 (notify).

steps.action: Enable notifications on 00000af7 via CCCD 00002902; also enable 00000af2 if health sync is wanted.
Send bind: 04 01 02 <sdk_int> 55 AA, zero-padded to 20 bytes, written to 00000af6.
steps.expect: Bind ack on 00000af7: same cmd/key, byte 2 = 0x00 on success.

steps.action: Write further 20-byte command/key frames to 00000af6 (e.g. real-time data = 02 A0; find-band = 06 04).

setup.notes: The band needs no provisioning and no pairing — the app protocol has no authentication anywhere (no bonding code paths in the app's BLE layer). The app scans for the 0xAF0 service, connects, enables notifications on 00000af7 (and 00000af2 for health sync) via the standard CCCD (00002902), then sends a bind command (cmd 0x04 key 0x01) whose payload carries a platform marker 0x02, the phone's Android API level, and the magic bytes 55 AA. Confidence medium: app-verified flow, partially observed on the wire by a third party, never replayed by this project.

rejoin.notes: The band joins no network and bonds with no client. Any client may connect once the previous one disconnects (the band accepts one connection at a time); "rebinding" is just the new client sending the bind frame — the app also offers an explicit unbind (cmd 0x04, key 0x02, payload 55 AA 55 AA).

testing.notes: No one on this project has driven an ID107-class band from this spec. All protocol facts are static analysis of the Veryfit 2.0 V2.0.37 APK (hash in header), cross-checked against a third-party on-wire GATT capture of a real ID107 HR band (g7smy.co.uk, 2017) which confirms the service/characteristic layout and one real-time-data frame — that supports per-fact `reported`, not this flag.

bind.description: Bind the band to this client. Payload observed in the app: byte 2 = 0x02 (platform marker, Android), byte 3 = the phone's Android API level (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT), bytes 4-5 = magic 55 AA; the band acks on af7 with the same cmd/key and byte 2 = 0x00 on success.

sdk_int.description: Client platform's Android API level as the vendor app emits it (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT; the app's own minimum is 18). No evidence the band validates it — 23 (Android 6.0) is a plausible default for this app generation.

find_band.description: App-control, key 0x04 ("search wristband"): makes the band alert (vibration/screen) so the user can locate it.

get_battery.description: Request battery level (get-info, key 0x05). Response field layout not established.

get_function_table.description: Request the band's function/feature table (get-info, key 0x02).

get_mac.description: Request the band's MAC address (get-info, key 0x04).

get_real_time.description: Request the band's real-time data (get-info, key 0xA0). The on-wire ID107 HR capture (g7smy.co.uk) shows the band's real-time frame on af7 as `02 a0 23 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 19 00 00 00 92 00 00 00 00 00` — little-endian 32-bit counters after the key byte (the first, 0x23 = 35, consistent with a step count), but the field assignment is NOT established; treat byte offsets as unknown.

incoming_call.description: Phone→band notification, key 0x01: signal an incoming call. Payload beyond the key (caller string encoding) is not established — an all-zero payload is the app's minimum frame, not a confirmed working notification.

one_key_restore.advanced_reason: Resets the band to factory state over the air, wiping the user profile, stored health history and bind state. The payload beyond the key byte is undocumented; what exactly is cleared is unknown. Recover by re-binding from the client afterwards.
one_key_restore.description: Settings, key 0x27: "one-key restore" — the app's over-the-air factory reset. Payload bytes beyond the key not established.

set_time.description: Settings, key 0x01: set the band's clock. The app builds the payload from the current date/time, but the byte layout of the payload was NOT recoverable with confidence (2026-07 review marked all payload formats unverifiable without an HCI snoop) — this entry documents the cmd/key only; do not send guessed bytes.

unbind.description: Unbind the band from the client (payload is the fixed magic 55 AA 55 AA, rest zero).

characteristics.name: Normal Write (command channel)
characteristics.notes: Command write characteristic (app's WRITE_UUID_NORMAL). All commands except health sync (cmd 0x08) are written here. Command IDs: firmware update 0x01, get-info 0x02, settings 0x03, bind/unbind 0x04, notify 0x05, app control 0x06, BLE control 0x07, dump-stack 0x20, log 0x21, restart 0xF0, factory 0xAA.

characteristics.name: Normal Notify (response channel)
characteristics.notes: Responses and band-initiated events for the af6 channel (app's NOTIFY_UUID_NORMAL; CCCD 00002902). Same 20-byte frame format: byte 0 echoes the command ID, byte 1 the key; success/failure status lives in the payload (e.g. bind ack byte 2 = 0x00 success; the app maps outcomes to bind-success 0x12 / unbind-success 0x14 internally).

characteristics.name: Health Write (health-sync command channel)
characteristics.notes: Health-data sync channel, write side (app's WRITE_UUID_HEALTH). The app routes every frame with command ID 0x08 here. Keys: sync request 0x01, sync success 0x02, data records sports-today 0x03 / sleep-today 0x04 / sports-history 0x05 / sleep-history 0x06 / heart-rate-today 0x07 / heart-rate-history 0x08, send-finished 0xEE, error 0xFF. Sync frames additionally carry a mode byte (safe 0x01 / other 0x00), a flag byte (foreground 0x01 / background 0x02) and a status (start 0x01 / resend 0x03 / end 0x02); their exact positions in the frame are not established.

characteristics.name: Health Notify (health-sync response channel)
characteristics.notes: Health-data sync channel, notify side (app's NOTIFY_UUID_HEALTH; CCCD 00002902). Carries the paged history records during sync.

services.name: Veryfit 2.0 Command Service
services.notes: Single vendor service carrying the whole protocol. Layout confirmed on a real ID107 HR by g7smy.co.uk (af6, af7+CCCD, af2+CCCD, af1 in that characteristic order) and in the app's BleGattAttributes (SERVICE_UUID=af0, WRITE_UUID_NORMAL=af6, NOTIFY_UUID_NORMAL=af7, WRITE_UUID_HEALTH=af1, NOTIFY_UUID_HEALTH=af2). Frame format: 20-byte fixed frames, zero-padded; byte 0 = command ID, byte 1 = key, bytes 2..19 = payload.

services.name: Nordic Legacy DFU Service
services.notes: Nordic legacy buttonless Device Firmware Update, used by the app for OTA (command ID 0x01 "ware update" hands off to it; the app bundles no.nordicsemi.android.dfu and declares its DfuService, and the UUID set 1530/1531/1532/1534 is what that library implements). Consistent with the nRF51822 hardware generation of the ID107-class bands. Reported presence only: the DFU characteristics appear while the band runs its bootloader — the on-wire capture of a normally-running ID107 HR shows no DFU service.
